exercise.passage_with_gaps:
When I was asked to play the piano at a local community event, I was both excited and nervous. It felt (0) _______________ early to perform in front of others, as I had only been learning for a few months. My initial (17) _______________ was to decline, but something stopped me. I remembered the (18) _______________ that had led me to start learning in the first place: a desire to play music for enjoyment. EARLY

I had begun taking lessons out of personal (19) _______________, expecting to make quick progress. However, the reality was different. Weeks of repetitive practice left me feeling (20) _______________ and close to giving up. But the invitation to play a simple accompaniment was a turning point.

On the day of the event, I made a small mistake during the performance. Surprisingly, it didn't ruin the (21) _______________. The music still added to the atmosphere and helped the group. This experience changed my (22) _______________ of success. It wasn't about being perfect but about contributing to something larger.

Afterwards, I continued practising with a new (23) _______________: to make music that others could enjoy, rather than striving for (24) _______________ perfection. It was a more fulfilling path.

The noun 'courage' is transformed into the adjective 'discouraged' to describe the feeling of wanting to give up.
The verb 'perform' is transformed into the noun 'performance' to refer to the act of playing music.
